```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(DesignComplexSurvival)
```

DesignComplexSurvival computes the operating characteristics of two-group
time-to-event trials analysed with the log-rank test, without patient-level
simulation. Each group follows a four-state model (progression-free,
progressed, switched, dead) with piecewise constant intensities. This
vignette shows a single endpoint with a delayed treatment effect, and then
overall survival (OS) with treatment switching after progression.

## A delayed treatment effect

The control group has exponential survival with a median of 12 months. In
the treatment group the hazard ratio is 1 for the first 6 months and 0.65
afterwards. Patients are enrolled at 10 per month for 3 months and at 30 per
month afterwards, and the dropout hazard is 0.003 per month in both groups.

```{r delayed-scenario}
lam <- log(2) / 12
ctl <- ms_model(death = lam, dropout = 0.003)
trt <- ms_model(time = c(0, 6), death = c(lam, 0.65 * lam), dropout = 0.003)
acc <- ms_accrual(time = c(0, 3), rate = c(10, 30))
scn <- ms_scenario(ctl, trt, allocation = 1, accrual = acc)
ev <- ms_events(scn, n = 700, calendar_time = c(12, 24, 36))
ev[, c("time", "enrolled", "events_control", "events_treatment", "events")]
```

With 700 patients, `r round(ev$events[3])` events are expected by month 36.

The design has interim analyses at 50 and 75 percent of the events, an
efficacy bound of O'Brien-Fleming type and a non-binding futility bound by
beta spending. `ms_size()` finds the number of events for a power of 90
percent.

```{r delayed-size}
looks <- ms_looks("os", fraction = c(0.5, 0.75, 1))
test <- ms_test(futility = "beta", sf_fut = "HSD", param_fut = -2)
des <- ms_size(scn, looks = looks, test = test, power = 0.9,
               solve_for = "events", n = 700)
des
```

The accrual ends at month `r round(des$accrual_duration, 1)`. The final
analysis needs `r des$events` events and takes place at month
`r round(des$study_duration, 1)`. The type I error is
`r signif(des$type1[["nonbinding"]], 3)` when the futility bounds are
ignored.

The mean of the standardized statistic can be computed directly from the
hazards (default) or with the Schoenfeld approximation, which uses the
event-weighted average of the log hazard ratio.

```{r delayed-mean}
t_fin <- des$study_duration
rbind(direct = lr_moments(scn, 700, t_fin)$z_mean,
      schoenfeld = lr_moments(scn, 700, t_fin, mean = "schoenfeld")$z_mean)
```

## Overall survival with switching after progression

In the control group the hazard of progression is 0.10 per month in the
first 4 months and 0.08 afterwards. At progression, 30 percent of the
patients switch to the experimental treatment; the others may switch later
with a hazard of 0.04 per month. After progression the hazard of death is
0.06 without switch and 0.035 after a switch. The treatment group has a
lower hazard of progression and no switching.

```{r switch-models}
ctl_sw <- ms_model(time = c(0, 4), prog = c(0.10, 0.08), death = 0.01,
                   switch_prob = 0.3, death_prog = 0.06, switch_rate = 0.04,
                   death_switch = 0.035, dropout = 0.003)
trt_sw <- ms_model(time = c(0, 4), prog = c(0.06, 0.05), death = 0.008,
                   death_prog = 0.055, dropout = 0.003)
ms_prob(ctl_sw, time = c(6, 12, 24))
```

The post-progression intensities are measured from the time of progression
(`clock = "reset"`, the default). OS and progression-free survival (PFS) of
the control group at 12 months are
`r round(ms_surv(ctl_sw, 12, "os")$surv, 3)` and
`r round(ms_surv(ctl_sw, 12, "pfs")$surv, 3)`.

```{r switch-power}
scn_sw <- ms_scenario(ctl_sw, trt_sw, accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 25))
pw <- ms_power(scn_sw, n = 500, looks = ms_looks("os", fraction = c(0.6, 1)),
               test = ms_test(), events = 300)
pw
```

With 300 OS events the power is `r round(pw$power, 3)`. Switching to the
experimental treatment in the control group moves the hazard ratio for OS
towards 1. For comparison, the same design without switching (all switching
intensities set to zero) has the power

```{r switch-none}
ctl_ns <- ms_model(time = c(0, 4), prog = c(0.10, 0.08), death = 0.01,
                   death_prog = 0.06, dropout = 0.003)
scn_ns <- ms_scenario(ctl_ns, trt_sw, accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 25))
pw_ns <- ms_power(scn_ns, n = 500, looks = ms_looks("os", fraction = c(0.6, 1)),
                  test = ms_test(), events = 300)
pw_ns$power
```

## Variance under the alternative

By default the standardized statistics have unit variances. With
`variance = "alternative"`, the variance and covariance of the score under
the alternative hypothesis (Luo et al. 2019) are used instead.

```{r alt-var}
mo_alt <- lr_moments(scn, n = 700, calendar_time = c(24, t_fin),
                     variance = "alternative")
mo_alt
```

Here the largest difference of the variances from 1 is
`r signif(max(abs(mo_alt$z_var - 1)), 2)`.

## References

Luo X, Mao X, Chen X, Qiu J, Bai S, Quan H (2019). Design and monitoring of
survival trials in complex scenarios. Statistics in Medicine 38:192-209.
